data.title: Anyone can build apps with AI. But who owns them?
data.ai_summary: A survey of 307 senior tech and security leaders found 44% lack a clear default for accountability when AI-generated tools cause production incidents. Most leaders see AI-driven building as a net productivity win, but governance remains uneven, with 78% describing it as manually maintained. The article argues for platform-level security controls to enforce accountability.
data.author: David Hsu

data.title: Best AI app builders in 2026: Comparing 9 platforms by price and iteration cost — TFN
data.ai_summary: Nine AI app builders are compared on iteration cost, with Softr ranked cheapest for running due to flat per-app-user pricing and credit-free editing. Other platforms charge credits or tokens per change, making them more expensive over time. Softr's MCP server lets users build from external AI agents without extra cost.

data.title: Claude and GPT Now Share Price Tags. Your Bill Still Won’t Match
data.ai_summary: OpenAI and Anthropic now share identical list prices for their top AI models, closing a 69-day price gap. However, nearly half of Anthropic's 2025 revenue came through cloud marketplaces, which OpenRouter's data misses. The article notes that actual bills still differ due to cache pricing and token usage.

data.title: Price War: OpenAI Wins Back Business Customers From Anthropic | Trending Topics

data.title: Risotto: IT-Agent löst bis zu 90 Prozent der Supporttickets automatisch

Risotto raised $10 million in seed funding to expand the agent.

Kilvin's agent builds tools from descriptions, and migration from Retool is supported.

data.title: How Much Does an MVP Cost to Build in 2026?
data.ai_summary: The article analyzes the bifurcated cost of building Minimum Viable Products (MVPs) in 2026, outlining four development paths ranging from $0 for no-code solutions to over $200,000 for agency-led builds. It highlights that AI coding tools have lowered technical barriers while user expectations have raised the ceiling for credible products in competitive markets. The piece emphasizes that founders are increasingly expected to build working MVPs before seeking pre-seed funding, citing StartupHub data on global startup financing trends.

data.title: The Best Lovable Alternatives for Agencies (and How to Pick One)
data.ai_summary: An industry consultant publishes a comparative guide ranking seven AI app-building platforms as alternatives to Lovable for agencies delivering production client work, recommending Zite as the strongest option due to its unlimited-user pricing, built-in database, and visually inspectable workflows that enable clean client handoffs. The article argues that the primary evaluation criterion for agency projects should be who maintains the app after delivery, not the speed of initial development, and includes detailed assessments of Bubble, Retool, Webflow, Bolt.new, v0, and Replit for specific use cases. The author predicts that within a year, the maintainability question will move to the forefront of agency tool purchasing decisions as more AI builders integrate real databases and readable logic generation.

data.title: Retool Review: The Fastest Way to Build Internal Apps?
data.ai_summary: The author reviews Retool, a low-code platform for building internal tools and dashboards, finding it delivers significant time savings by combining drag-and-drop UI building with custom code flexibility. The review praises Retool's universal integrations, AI-powered app generation, enterprise-grade security, and support for developer workflows. However, it notes the platform requires technical knowledge (SQL, JavaScript), is not suitable for customer-facing products, and can become expensive as team size scales, ultimately giving it a 4.5/5 rating and 'MobileAppDaily Approved' status.
